relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: Our results in sural nerve showed that the expression of TLR4 and TNFα correlated with each other and with the NRS, indicating a connection to the development of neuropathic pain.

relationships.subject: TLR4
relationships.evidence_quote: The NF-κB-mediated pathway can be activated by the stimulation of TLR4 with a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), resulting in the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα

relationships.subject: SIRT1
relationships.evidence_quote: SIRT1 is able to deacetylate NF-κB, and its downregulation would imply an upregulation of the NF-κB pathway, explaining the high expression of TNFα

relationships.subject: HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: It is likely that the amount of endogenous TLR4 ligands, like high mobility group box1 (HMGB1), is increased in painful neuropathy, binding to TLR4 and leading to the activation of the NF-κB pro-inflammatory cascade and the upregulation of TNFα

key_findings: In sural nerve of polyneuropathy patients, TLR4 and TNFα expression correlated with pain NRS, and TNFα was upregulated in severe pain with inflammatory neuropathy.
TRPV1 and SIRT1 were downregulated in inflammatory versus non-inflammatory PNP; TLR4 and miR-146a-5p were lower in distal than proximal skin.
